note: v1 80.68 (seeds 0/11 80.68/80.65), Crate Dig, the opener: a beat-tape intro where a soul-jazz record is found and flipped on an MPC in front of you (86 bpm). chop-souljazz's 16 quarter-note slices play as found (muffled, wobbling, like a record in the next room), then re-sequenced into two-bar flips with a boom-bap kick and snare and a sub, a physical tenor sax answering the chops in C mixolydian, a stutter build on one slice (quarters, eighths, sixteenths), a harder flip with split eighth stabs and the sax an octave up, and the record as found again as it lifts. compscore's sections are the open problem: with four-bar flips every block reads as a section (12, structure 38), with two-bar flips the whole middle reads as one (3 sections, recurrence 13.5).

v2 94.97 (seeds 0/11 94.97/94.76 vs v1 80.68/80.65): THE DIG - the middle gets the section turn it lacked. After the sax section the beat falls away for four bars and the record is found again: the muffled loop in its original order (like the opening) under the sax alone, before the stutter build drags the flip back. The opener now reads as found -> flipped -> found -> stuttered -> flipped harder -> found, so its returns are heard (sections 3 -> 5, recurrence 13.5 -> 100, structure 100).

v3 97.04 (seeds 0/11 97.04/97.03 vs v2 94.97/94.75): the opener's MIX, against the lo-fi envelope. The flipped soul-jazz record was missing its body - 290-470 Hz sat 5-11 dB under the album's references because the master was cutting 220 Hz - while the sub pushed 70-85 Hz 8 dB over and the deep 38 Hz was thin. Now the master cuts 78 Hz, lifts 330 Hz (the record's warmth: the horns and the keys inside the chops) and adds weight at 40 Hz: spectrum 90.5 -> 97, cohesion with the album 70 -> 100. The record sounds like it is in the room now, not just the beat.

v4 96.93 (seeds 0/11 96.93/96.94 vs v3 97.04/97.03): THE TURNTABLE. The album now starts with the record spinning up to speed - the master's tape-stop held for the first two beats and released, so the soul-jazz sample drags in from below pitch like a deck coming up - and the opener ends with the record spinning down as it lifts (the stop engaged over the last bar). The record-as-found sections (the start, the dig, the end) also wear their own worn vinyl (wM's vinyl fx: crackle, dust, warp 8, wear .6) on top of the muffle, so the found record and the flipped beat sound like two different objects.

v5 96.93 (seeds 0/11 96.93/96.93, level with v4): THE FLIP OF THE FLIP, with wM's chop fx. The beat-tape intro is about resampling, so now the resampled beat gets resampled again: the last bar of the flip, of the sax section and of the hard flip is cut from the chops' own previous bar into eight slices and replayed out of order (0 r1 2 2 . r5 6 _ - a reversed hit, a doubled slice, a live beat, a dropped one), the producer's hand on the pads closing each phrase before the next section. Measured: those bars differ from v4 by about 4-6 dB under their level.
